findings.text: PRIOR BLOCK CLOSED (the central question). The escalate that blocked WARP-1103 was that the mandatory placement gate PLAN-0011 assigns to W3 in three present-tense places (O3.measure 'a spec without a placement resolving to a contract area cannot reach ready and is never claimed'; the W3 text 'the validator refuses a ready spec without a resolving placement ... a footprint that creates a module or crosses a boundary raises the risk tier'; RJ2 'a placeless spec never reaches ready and is never claimed') was deferred - only an OPTIONAL structural declaration shipped. The completion builds exactly the missing gate as ONE pure predicate arch.placement_gate consumed at all three transition/claim points (check_ready + `ready` CLI, frontier.claimable, plan.cmd_run_check), plus the footprint->tier rule (footprint_tier_floor over area_for_path), the elaboration-skill ask, and the no-corpus-sweep guard. I proved each plan clause with my own commands (clauses a-e above). O3, the W3 text, and RJ2 are now satisfied. Zero blocking findings.

TIER-RULE / SELF-ELEVATION JUDGMENT (not blocking): the self-elevation to risk:high + human_approval:required is CORRECT and sound dogfooding. WARP-1103's footprint genuinely edits files in two declared areas - contracts (arch.py, validate.py, plan.py) and fleet (frontier.py) - so by its own footprint_tier_floor rule (>=2 areas -> floor high) and NG2 (the machine never LOWERS a tier, only raises), declaring high + required approval is the honest, conservative outcome; the spec's own rule classifies the spec. CALIBRATION OBSERVATION (non-blocking): the rule equates 'footprint spans 2+ declared areas' with 'crosses a boundary'. That is a defensible elaboration-time proxy for the plan's W3 language and it fails toward MORE scrutiny (never less), consistent with NG2 - but spanning two areas via an allow-listed dependency edge (fleet->contracts IS allowed here) is a breadth signal, not an architectural violation, so a small, correctly-layered two-area edit is also elevated to high+approval. This is conservative and not wrong; the precise boundary-violation / new-module distinction honestly needs the diff and is deferred to W2. Flagged as a calibration note for the W2/W4 builders, not a defect.

HONESTY (NG5) - accurate. The deferrals are stated honestly and consistently in the spec Out of scope, the arch.py docstrings, the AC text, the capabilities entry, and the commit message: enforcing the declared footprint against the actual diff and detecting a genuinely-new module are WARP-1102 (W2, needs the diff), and grading shape-fit is WARP-1104 (W4). Neither is claimed here. The capabilities entry (spec_placement_footprint, status: mechanical, home .warp/arch.py) accurately describes a shipped mechanical gate whose teeth I reproduced; nothing is marked mechanizable that nothing enforces. check_placement short-circuits at a presence-gate before loading arch, so the corpus is untouched with no per-spec cost inflation.

GATE-SCOPE OBSERVATION (non-blocking, consistent with the design): once a placement is declared, placement_gate also requires a well-formed footprint and refuses any unresolvable area even if another placement entry resolves. This is slightly stricter than the literal AC6 phrasing ('a placement that resolves') but is the intended fail-closed posture (a placement implies a footprint; an unresolvable area is a real error) and matches validate_placement, so the two layers agree. It only ever rejects, never admits, so it cannot mask a defect.

ENVIRONMENTAL PARITY (non-blocking, general to WARP commits): the 'generated' gate check is green because specs/index.md was regenerated at this commit; a rerun on a later day flips it RED until restamped - the same date-stamp behavior recorded in prior WARP-100x/1101/1105 reviews. After all my runs the tree is clean: HEAD remains 84fc55d, WARP-1103 stays draft, and the only working-tree changes are the expected uncommitted proof/WARP-1103/ plus .warp/events.jsonl and .warp/last_verify.

summary: WARP-1103 (placement and footprint at elaboration, W3 of PLAN-0011) PASSES WITH NOTES at 84fc55d, ZERO blocking findings, and the prior BLOCK is genuinely CLOSED. The completion builds the missing mandatory gate as one pure predicate arch.placement_gate enforced at all three plan-mandated points and NEVER as a corpus sweep: the ready transition (validate.check_ready + `ready` CLI, run by /warp:spec), the claim (frontier.claimable filters a placeless build unit), and the build (plan.cmd_run_check). I proved each PLAN-0011 clause (O3.measure, the W3 text, RJ2) with my own commands: a real shipped placeless spec (WARP-0100) still passes check_spec (rc 0) yet check_ready refuses it (rc 1); a placeless build unit is excluded from claimable while a placed one is claimable and a review unit is not gated; run-check refuses a placeless and an under-tiered 2-area spec and clears placed ones; the elaboration skill now asks for both fields; and the footprint->tier rule refuses a 2-area footprint below high and passes it at high/critical, with valid multi-area placements at the correct tier passing (no over-refusal). Adoption safe everywhere (no contract -> the whole gate stands down; verify.sh stays green over the 107-spec corpus with zero migration; validate.py all rc 0 over 108). The gate is GREEN (selftest 1583/0), the engine is byte-identical across all 8 copies (template sync + pack drift pass), there is no import cycle (frontier->validate is the allow-listed fleet->contracts edge), RULE #1 is clean, no protected path is touched, and the manifest proof_digest recomputes to sha256:6bb89f7b3ed53cb1. The spec's self-elevation to risk:high + human_approval:required is correct, sound dogfooding of its own footprint->tier rule (it edits frontier.py, spanning contracts+fleet). Five non-blocking notes: block-closed confirmation; a calibration observation that 'spans 2 areas' is a conservative proxy for 'crosses a boundary'; honest W2/W4 deferrals; a fail-closed gate-scope observation; and standard index date-stamp parity. Verdict: pass_with_notes. The spec is left draft; nothing landed or pushed.
